content:
Vivek Kulkarni: Dropping a quick roll-up of feature asks we’re hearing in regulated ABM convos (finserv + healthcare) so we can triage: roadmap vs enablement/docs. Sources: NorthBridge pilot check-ins, Brightline security review, Regal Wealth deep dive, Helix scoping.

Top themes (Private/Dedicated):
1) Audit log exports (formats + destinations)
- “We need audit logs in our SIEM” (Splunk / Sentinel / QRadar)
- Ask: first-class exporters (S3 bucket, Splunk HEC, syslog/TCP) vs “we’ll ship it ourselves”
- Ask: JSON schema doc + example payloads + versioning (so they can write parsers)
- Ask: include authz changes + key events (SAML config changes, user/role updates), not just API requests

2) Retention controls + deletion semantics
- Ask: configurable retention window for request metadata/logs (7/30/90/365) + “no retention” modes
- Ask: clarity on who stores what in Private (their storage) vs Dedicated (Redwood-managed) + how deletion requests work
- Ask (finserv): WORM/immutability wording comes up a lot; they want tamper-evident story

3) Installer / upgrade UX for Private
- Air-gapped installs: offline images, pinned dependencies
- Preflight checks: GPU driver/CUDA compatibility, disk sizing, ports, TLS cert validation
- Upgrade path: “how do we do minor upgrades without downtime” + rollback

My initial proposal:
- Near-term (pilot unblockers): docs + examples + an “official” audit log schema + reference exporter patterns
- Roadmap candidates: first-class S3 exporter + retention policy controls in control plane + installer preflight

Would love reactions from Security + SE + PMM: what’s required to win vs nice-to-have? :point_down:

Naomi Feldman: +1 on capturing this. Two notes from Security side:
1) Please avoid “immutable logs” / “WORM” as a blanket claim. We can say “exportable audit logs” + “integrity controls” only if we can back it up.
2) We keep getting asked “are you HIPAA-ready?” (esp. Helix). We should stick to the approved language: “supports HIPAA-aligned deployments” / “can sign BAA for eligible plans” only when Legal confirms. Don’t let the roadmap bullet accidentally turn into an external promise.

Markus Klein: From SE calls:
- Brightline + Regal Wealth both said: if we don’t have *an easy path* to get logs into Splunk, they’ll assume it’s a science project.
- They’re okay with a sidecar approach for Private (Fluent Bit / Vector) as long as we provide:
  a) exact fields they’ll get
  b) sample configs
  c) clarity on volume/throughput (events/sec) so they can size it

Also: “audit log export” keeps getting mixed up with “request/response logging”. They want audit logs (who did what, when) more than payload logging.

Fatima Noor: +1. In NorthBridge week-1 checkin we got very specific requests:
- “JSONL to S3, partitioned by day, in our bucket”
- consistent `actor`, `action`, `resource`, `result`, `ip`, `request_id`, `tenant`, `timestamp` fields
- they asked for “export latency” (e.g., within 5 min) and “no gaps” guarantees

We should be careful: for the pilot we can do best-effort export pattern, but SLOs need to be explicit and conservative.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated angle: some of these are actually packaging/positioning problems.
- Dedicated customers assume Redwood stores logs unless told otherwise.
- We need a simple matrix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: who has control of retention, where logs live, what’s configurable.

If we can’t build exporter X right now, give Sales an approved answer: “We support export via <pattern>” and point to a doc.

Soojin Lee: From PMM perspective, agree we need the matrix + “what’s true today” language.
We should also separate:
- “Evidence pack / security FAQ” (what we can assert)
- “Roadmap” (what we can hint at only in 1:1 and with caveats)

If we’re going to publish an audit log schema, we need Security review on the field list (make sure we don’t accidentally suggest we log prompts/outputs by default).

Olga Petrov: For questionnaires, the top recurring questions are literally copy/paste:
- “Describe audit logging (events captured, retention, access controls, export mechanism)”
- “Can customer configure retention and delete data on request?”
- “Provide sample audit log entries”

If we can create a standardized answer + attachments, it will save us a ton of time in the next 4–6 weeks.

Kira Thompson: On docs side, I can take a first pass at:
- Audit log schema page + sample payloads (clearly labeled: “representative example”)
- “Export patterns” page for Private: Fluent Bit + Vector examples (Splunk HEC + S3)

But I’ll need engineering to confirm what fields/events are actually emitted today in Private vs Dedicated.

Elliot Price: +1. Also please keep docs phrasing tight:
- Avoid “compliant with X” unless we have explicit sign-off
- Prefer “supports” / “enables” language

If we’re publishing configs, include a section called “Customer responsibilities” (SIEM endpoint config, key rotation, storage retention, etc.).

Vivek Kulkarni: Super helpful. Proposed triage (tell me where I’m wrong):

A) Enablement / docs (do now, supports ABM)
- Publish audit log event schema + versioning guidance (v1)
- Add 2 exporter reference snippets for Private (Splunk HEC + S3) using sidecar/agent approach
- Add “Deployment mode responsibility matrix” (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) for retention + logs
- Standard questionnaire answer pack (Olga/Naomi review)

B) Roadmap candidates (need sizing + prioritization)
- First-class export destination in Private (S3 to start) with basic delivery guarantees
- Retention policy controls surfaced in Private control plane (configurable windows + delete semantics)
- Installer improvements: offline bundle + preflight checks

C) Not committing (capture, but don’t promise)
- “Immutable/WORM logs” as a product feature (needs deeper design + legal positioning)

Action items:
- @Kira Thompson @Elliot Price can you draft the doc outline + list of “fields we must confirm” by EOW?
- @Naomi Feldman @Olga Petrov can you mark which questionnaire answers need evidence pack links vs “narrative answer”?
- @Markus Klein @Fatima Noor please drop any exact prospect quotes/requirements we should bake into the schema/export docs.

Naomi Feldman: Works. I’ll also add a note: if we provide sample payloads, include a redaction guidance snippet (what customers should/shouldn’t log) to avoid us being seen as recommending storing PHI/PCI.

Markus Klein: I’ll paste the Regal Wealth ask list here (sanitized):
- “syslog to our collector” (preferred)
- “Splunk HEC acceptable”
- they want to filter by `event_type` and `severity`
- they asked if we can export to CloudWatch (they’re AWS-heavy)

Fatima Noor: NorthBridge specific: they asked for “change history” for auth config (SAML metadata updates, cert rotations). Even if we can’t do all of it, make sure schema includes a placeholder event type so we don’t paint ourselves into a corner.

Lauren Bishop: Can we also align on what Sales should say *today* when asked “Can I set retention to 0?” There’s some confusion.

Vivek Kulkarni: Yes—let’s handle that as part of the matrix + a Sales snippet.
I’ll draft proposed wording and route to PMM + Security for approval before it goes anywhere.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: Also suggest we link these new docs from the regulated landing page + security FAQ (so it’s discoverable without Sales having to hunt).

Kira Thompson: Got it. I’ll start an outline doc and tag eng to confirm current behavior. Once confirmed, I can turn it into a docs PR.

Olga Petrov: I’ll compile top 10 questionnaire prompts we’ve seen in the last month and map them to the new docs pages / evidence pack artifacts.

Vivek Kulkarni: Great. I’ll open internal tickets for B) items with “ABM feedback” context and we’ll prioritize in next product triage. For now, let’s treat A) as the unblockers for the pilot.

(added reaction) Naomi Feldman: :white_check_mark:
(added reaction) Markus Klein: :thumbsup:
